title: A finite set in one graded piece defining a finitely presented Proj quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ a commutative unital nonnegatively graded $R$-algebra, so $R\to A_0$ is part of the data [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Let $I=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I_n\subseteq A$ be a homogeneous ideal, meaning $I_n=I\cap A_n$ and $A_mI_n\subseteq I_{m+n}$. Assume $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj] is quasi-compact and the quotient-induced closed immersion $\operatorname{Proj}(A/I)\hookrightarrow P$ [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] is of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exist $d>0$ and a finite list $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in I_d$, with $r\geq0$, such that, putting $F=Rg_1+\cdots+Rg_r\subseteq I_d$ and writing $FA$ for its generated homogeneous ideal, the quotient-induced closed subschemes of $P$ satisfy $$\operatorname{Proj}(A/FA)=\operatorname{Proj}(A/I).$$ No finite generation of $A$ over $R$ or $A_0$, of $I$, or of any component $A_n$ is assumed, and $R\to A_0$ need not be an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0802, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj-finite, proof on an affine base: choose the numerators inside the prescribed homogeneous ideal I and put them in one positive degree. This formulation keeps that ideal as input; it does not assert the separate homogeneous-ideal recovery theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion] (0), the positive homogeneous standard opens cover $P$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover $P=\bigcup_{i=1}^tD_+(f_i)$, with $f_i\in A_{a_i}$ and $a_i>0$. If $P$ is empty, take $d=1$ and the empty list: both closed subschemes are empty. Henceforth $t>0$. Put $Z=\operatorname{Proj}(A/I)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_P\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$. The ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal], the hypothesis on $i$ implies that $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type; that lemma requires neither Noetherianity nor separatedness of $P$.

source.place: Tag 0802, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj-finite, finite standard-open cover and finite type of the ideal; Tag 01TV, morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation.

proof.text: For any homogeneous ideal $H\subseteq A$, give $C=A/H$ its quotient grading and denote images by bars. Every positive homogeneous element of $C$ lifts to one of $A$, so $C_+$ equals the image-generated irrelevant ideal. Thus [lem-sfb-proj-map-standard-charts] applies to $A\twoheadrightarrow C$: over $D_+(f)$ the quotient closed immersion has chart map $q_f:A_{(f),0}\to C_{(\bar f),0}$ sending $h/f^e$ to $\bar h/\bar f^e$. This map is surjective, since a numerator in $C_{ea}$ lifts to $A_{ea}$, where $a=\deg f$. Its kernel is exactly the set of fractions $h/f^e$ with $h\in H\cap A_{ea}$. Indeed, if $b/f^e$ maps to zero, the localization relation [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $f^k b\in H$ for some $k\geq0$, and $b/f^e=(f^k b)/f^{e+k}$; the converse is immediate. The numerator is homogeneous of degree $(e+k)a$. These kernel fractions form an ideal. With $H=I$, this kernel is precisely $K_f=\mathcal J(D_+(f))$.

source.place: Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj (2), and the quotient/localization relation; the same chart kernel is used in the affine proof of Tag 0802.

proof.text: The standard chart $D_+(f_i)$ is affine by [def-pc-proj]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a) to $\mathcal J$ there. It gives a finite generating list for the $A_{(f_i),0}$-ideal $K_{f_i}$. By step 2 and [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], each generator has the form $h_{ij}/f_i^{e_{ij}}$ with $h_{ij}\in I\cap A_{e_{ij}a_i}$. Replacing numerator and denominator by $f_i h_{ij}$ and $f_i^{e_{ij}+1}$ if necessary, take every $e_{ij}>0$, without changing any fraction or its membership in $I$. A zero ideal may have the empty generating list.

source.place: Tag 0802, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj-finite, homogeneous numerators h_{i,j,k}; Properties Tag 01PB, lemma-finite-type-module.

proof.text: Let $L=\prod_{i=1}^t a_i>0$ and let $E$ be the maximum of $0$ and all the finitely many $e_{ij}$. Set $d=L(E+1)>0$. Then $a_i\mid d$ and $d/a_i\geq e_{ij}$ for every pair. Define $$g_{ij}=h_{ij}f_i^{d/a_i-e_{ij}}\in I_d.$$ The degree equality is $e_{ij}a_i+(d/a_i-e_{ij})a_i=d$, and ideal membership follows from $h_{ij}\in I$. Take $F$ to be the $R$-span of this finite family, and $H=FA$. The degree-zero image of $R$ makes this an $R$-submodule of $I_d$, and $H\subseteq I$ is homogeneous: decomposing each coefficient into its homogeneous components decomposes every sum of products with a $g_{ij}$ into elements of $H$.

source.place: Tag 0802, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj-finite, choose a common positive degree and multiply h by a power of f; on the affine base F is the finite R-span.

proof.text: Fix $i$. Applying the kernel description of step 2 to $H$ gives an ideal $K'_{f_i}\subseteq K_{f_i}$ because $H\subseteq I$. On the other hand, for every chosen generator of $K_{f_i}$, $$h_{ij}/f_i^{e_{ij}}=g_{ij}/f_i^{d/a_i}\in K'_{f_i}.$$ The equality follows by multiplying numerator and denominator by $f_i^{d/a_i-e_{ij}}$. Hence every generator lies in $K'_{f_i}$ and $K'_{f_i}=K_{f_i}$. This uses all chosen $g_{ij}$ together: those coming from other charts cause no problem because they too lie in $I$.

source.place: Tag 0802, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj-finite, final assertion that the constructed F is a solution: equality of chart ideals.

proof.text: By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] (3), the homogeneous quotient $A\twoheadrightarrow A/H$ gives a closed subscheme of $P$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], on the affine chart $D_+(f_i)$ this closed subscheme is defined by the kernel $K'_{f_i}$; the original $Z$ is defined by $K_{f_i}$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], both ideal sheaves restrict on this affine chart to the associated sheaves of these kernel ideals. Step 5 therefore identifies their restrictions and their quotient structure sheaves. The charts cover $P$, so the ideal subsheaves agree (sections agree if they agree after restriction to a cover). Thus $\operatorname{Proj}(A/FA)=\operatorname{Proj}(A/I)$ as closed subschemes of $P$. Enumerating the $g_{ij}$ gives the required finite list, including the empty list if every $K_{f_i}=0$.
